summary: This PR only adds a test (tests/supervisor_merge_detection_test.sh), a documentation/patch archive (ai-os/patches/supervisor-entrypoint-merge-report-fix-2026-07-24.diff), and a PROGRESS.md update -- it does not itself contain a diff to scripts/supervisor-entrypoint.sh because that script lives outside this git repo, on the server at /opt/veridian/scripts/supervisor-entrypoint.sh, which matches this repo's established convention (14 prior ai-os/patches/*.diff entries archiving out-of-repo server script changes, including three prior supervisor-entrypoint.sh patches). I independently verified this is not a bare self-report: the live server file at /opt/veridian/scripts/supervisor-entrypoint.sh actually contains the MERGE-DETECTION-BLOCK-START/END markers and matches the archived patch exactly (diffed against /tmp/orig/supervisor-entrypoint.sh); I ran the new test file against that real live script and all 3 scenarios passed; and I ran it against the pre-fix backup, which correctly fails (no markers found), confirming the test discriminates real behavior rather than being tautological. The root cause (gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch's combined exit code going non-zero on a local worktree branch-delete conflict even though the API-side merge had already succeeded) and the fix (split merge from best-effort branch deletion via the GitHub API, judge success solely via a fresh gh pr view --json state,mergedAt call) are architecturally sound and fail in the safe direction: any ambiguity (e.g. a transient gh pr view failure right after a real merge) defaults to blocked, never to a false completed. Variable usage ($REPO, $BRANCH, hardcoded FChecklist owner) matches existing conventions used elsewhere in the same script (PR creation/lookup). No .github/workflows/** files are touched. This is additive-only (new test, new patch archive, docs) with no schema/migration/auth/payment paths touched, correctly tier1.
